text.title: Program Dependency Aging Chart Recipe — Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Does the program have at least 3 teams, a typed dependency graph with tracker link timestamps, a weekly checkpoint, and a named program PM?

branch.when: teams_count < 3 OR graph_present == false OR cadence_weekly == false OR named_pm == false
branch.conclusion: Skip. A single team has nothing to age across; without a graph build it first (see `dependency-graph-reasoning`); a monthly cadence sees the rot after the milestone slipped.

branch.when: teams_count >= 3 AND graph_present == true AND cadence_weekly == true AND named_pm == true
branch.question: Does every plotted edge carry producer, consumer, type, `opened_at`, `needed_by` and a tracker link id, and are standup-only dependencies absent?

branch.conclusion: Block. Complete the edges in the graph and create edges for the dependencies only mentioned in standups.

branch.question: Is age computed from each edge's `opened_at`, in the bands fixed at adoption, with re-ticketed edges inheriting the original `opened_at`?

branch.conclusion: Recompute age from `opened_at` in the adopted bands; regenerate the last four weeks.
Link the new edges to their originals and inherit `opened_at`.

branch.when: age_clock == opened_at AND bands_changed_since_adoption == false AND reticketed_edges_without_superseded_from == 0
branch.question: Does every edge in an escalation band or with non-positive slack carry an owner and a due date, with a re-baseline decision on every edge over 28 days?

branch.conclusion: Assign owner and date to each; program PM decides re-baseline for the top band before the checkpoint closes.
Regenerate by script, publish the chart with the SLE line and the sorted action table, close the checkpoint.
